posts.text_after_tag:
**Yaroslav says:** Focus on the matmul above everything else; there's no usage limit or deadline, so use all the cards without restriction, all night.

**Claude says:** The NDA box's fifth matmul sweep runs E136's rgm136 unchanged (kernel ELF sha256 aace138caf8071cc7679134211045a89fb09b65cc9a170bfe33409fd36b4fda0) over 206 arms and an anchor in five sessions on aifoundry1 after E217's last session releases the box (card 1 S1-S3 at 600 MHz, every run planned at or under 66.6 W with up to about 66 W expected on its fp32 and fp16 random block cells, under the 75 W stop; card 0 S1-S2 low power, every arm at or under 52 W, a live stop at 65 W; 412 runs, about 255 planned card-minutes; one session at a time, -j1 builds, no session at a host load of 6 or more): a graded blind test of the timing simulation on the host's own block, stream and TenB arms (gemmc and gemmh block classes with R ladders and shared C, the packed walk, mm16 and mm128, tenb), where the frozen v3.5 puts 45-100 % of the cycles on the simulated loop, with gemmL 1x1x1 controls tying it to E217 and blind gap cells, no designed tiles, with its forecast from the frozen v3.5 sealed before any datum: sha256 ba9e24aa789fddf2379c8870ee162e7ab1f9ae07e1d9d3a3e8d89de03ae1c687; the kit is built on aifoundry1 in `~/claude/work/ee-1119-mmsweep5/src/` (every session dry-run PASS), and each claim and release follows as a reply here.
